body:
Ted may have denied dating any girl in high school, but he has never denied
"asking" for a date. There's a difference.

If you believe that Ted's intellectual pretensions are anything other than a
smokescreen for his undying hatred of anyone who has anything that he wants
but can't get on account of his social pathology then you are simply another
one of Ted's dupes.

And Zodiac never made any references to drugs. That was a fanciful invention
of Robert Graysmith. Zodiac's missives were straightforward, terse, and very
cogent.

And maybe it's only coincidence, but every one of Zodiac's victims was taken
from behind. Incidentally, regarding Ted's modus operandi, you should have a
look at the Psych Report and the Chris Waites book. They'll open your eyes.

Pyro 1488 wrote in message <19991029143041.04443.00000050@ng-fo1.aol.com>...
>Mignarda wrote:
>
>>The thing that really ices it for me is that Ted's personality and his
>>motivation for killing are exactly the same as Zodiac's--he's just the
sort
>>of personality you'd expect Zodiac to be, murdering to make a statement
and
>>to get publicity. Time will tell.
>
>Not really.  The Unabomber has always held intellectual pretensions and has
>used his anti-technology views as a front for what was essentially a
>sociopathic outburst.  The Zodiac, on the other hand, has never openly
given
>his political or philosophical views; on one letter to the SFPD he stated
he
>wanted vengeance for having been rejected by so many females in high
school,
>etc.  I don't recall any stories of TK asking out any girls in HS.
Moreover,
>the Zodiac faced his victims up close, whereas TK sent mailbombs.  IIRC, in
his
>letters the Zodiac killer even made references to drugs; TK is not known to
>have used drugs, as far as I know.
>
>Regards,
>Pyro
>--
>
>"Given the past history of leftism, it would be utterly foolish for
non-leftist
>revolutionaries today to collaborate with leftists." (Para. 217)
>
